ArrangementCalculator.count:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Calculates the number of permutations P(n, m) by returning n! directly when m is absent or equals n, and computing n! // (n-m)! otherwise." count]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> n </REF>: int "The total number of distinct items in the pool."
        <REF> m </REF>: int "The number of items to arrange; defaults to None, meaning all n items are arranged."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "The permutation count: n! when m is None or equals n, otherwise n! divided by (n-m)! using integer floor division."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Evaluate whether m is None or n equals m; if either condition is true via short-circuit or, take the if branch and return ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n) immediately as the full permutation count. RESULT factorial_result]
            [COMMAND If neither short-circuit condition was satisfied, enter the else branch: call ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n) to obtain n!, call ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n - m) to obtain (n-m)!, then compute their integer floor division and return the result as P(n, m). RESULT permutation_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: m is None — the caller did not supply a second argument, meaning all n items are to be arranged.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n) directly, skipping the division path entirely. RESULT factorial_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: n equals m — the number of items to arrange equals the pool size, making the result mathematically identical to n!.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n) directly, skipping the division path entirely. RESULT factorial_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.count_all:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the total number of arrangements of n elements taken 1 through n at a time by summing ArrangementCalculator.count(n, i) for each subset size i from 1 to n inclusive." count_all]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> n </REF>: int "The total number of elements available for arrangement; determines both the upper bound of the summation loop and the first argument passed to ArrangementCalculator.count on each iteration"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> total </REF>: int "The sum of ArrangementCalculator.count(n, i) for every i from 1 to n inclusive, representing the total count of all non-empty arrangements of n elements"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize accumulator variable total to 0 as the additive identity before any summation begins RESULT total]
            [COMMAND Iterate i over the inclusive integer range [1, n]: for each value of i, call ArrangementCalculator.count(n, i) and add the returned value to total RESULT total]
            [COMMAND Return total as the final accumulated sum of all arrangement counts RESULT total]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.select:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Generates all permutations of length m from the instance's data list, defaulting to the full length when m is not provided." select]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> m </REF>: int or None "Number of elements per permutation; defaults to the total length of self.datas when not provided"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list of lists "A list containing every distinct ordered permutation of m elements drawn from self.datas, each permutation represented as a list"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether m is None; if so, set m to the length of self.datas so that all elements are used in each permutation RESULT m]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty list to collect the permutation results RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Iterate over every permutation of exactly m elements drawn from self.datas using itertools.permutations RESULT permutation]
            [COMMAND Within the permutations loop, convert each permutation tuple to a list and append it to result RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return result containing all collected permutations RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: m is not supplied by the caller (m is None)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Set m to len(self.datas) so that the full dataset length is used as the permutation size RESULT m]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.select_all:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Iterates over all 1-based indices of the internal data list and collects every result returned by calling select on each index into a single flat list." select_all]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list "A flat list containing all items returned by select for every valid index in datas"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty list named result to accumulate all selected items RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Iterate over i from 1 to len(self.datas) inclusive (i.e., range(1, len(self.datas) + 1)), and for each value of i extend result with the return value of self.select(i) RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return result after the loop has completed all iterations RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.factorial:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the factorial of a non-negative integer n by iteratively multiplying all integers from 2 through n inclusive, returning 1 for n less than 2." factorial]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> n </REF>: integer "The non-negative integer whose factorial is to be computed"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: integer "The factorial of n, i.e. the product of all positive integers from 1 to n; equals 1 when n is 0 or 1"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize result to the integer constant 1 RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Iterate i over the integer range starting at 2 and ending at n inclusive (i.e. range(2, n + 1)); for each value of i, multiply result by i and store the product back into result RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return result RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
